messages.subject: heterosceasticity / non-constant variance
parts:
Hi,

I'm very new to inla, and I have a pretty basic question. I've attached a very basic MWE below.
Does anyone know the syntax for modelling non-constant variance? I.e. having scale ~ x as well as only the mean (in a gaussian example, or modelling the shape and scale separately in a gamma example, etc.)

I've attached an example below to show what I mean, as an example for where we would want the variance to change with x:

library(INLA)

library(ggplot2)

x <- seq(0,1, len = 100)
y <- rnorm(length(x), 1+ 2*x, sd = x)
plot(x,y)

data <- data.frame(x, y)

model <- inla(y ~ x,  data = data)

pred = model$summary.fitted.values[, c("0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant") ]

ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y))+
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y=pred$`0.5quant`))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin=pred$`0.025quant`, ymax = pred$`0.975quant`), alpha = 0.25)



(also, as a side note, how do we get out the predictions for the response, rather than just the predictions for the mean? I know how to sample from the posterior, but that seems like a pretty slow way of getting prediction intervals haha)


Cheers,
Evan

if the scaling of the precision is know, this is option 'scale'; see
inla.doc("^gaussian")

for a regression model on log(precision), this needs to be implemented.
